probes.label: behavior
probes.prompt: Riverbend Community Health Center in Dover, Delaware runs a diabetes management program that enrolled 412 patients in 2024 and retained 268 of them through the twelve-month mark. The program is staffed by two nurse educators and one part-time dietitian, and it is funded by a state grant of $185,000 that expires in June. Average HbA1c among completers fell from 9.1 to 7.8. The board's finance committee has asked whether the program should be renewed at current staffing, expanded to the Milford satellite clinic, or wound down. Write a short memo from program director Amara Osei to the finance committee laying out what the program did this year, what the numbers show about retention and clinical results, what renewal at each level would cost, and what the committee needs to decide before the grant lapses.
probes.response:
**MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Finance Committee, Board of Directors, Riverbend Community Health Center
**FROM:** Amara Osei, Program Director, Diabetes Management Program
**RE:** Diabetes Management Program — Year in Review and Renewal Options

---

**1. What the program did this year**

The Diabetes Management Program enrolled 412 patients in 2024. Staffing consisted of two full-time nurse educators and one part-time dietitian, supported by a $185,000 state grant that expires June 30. Patients received individual education sessions, group classes, dietary counseling, medication review, and regular HbA1c monitoring over a twelve-month course.

**2. What the numbers show**

*Retention.* Of the 412 patients enrolled, 268 completed the full twelve months, a retention rate of 65 percent. The remaining 144 (35 percent) left the program before the twelve-month mark. We are still analyzing the reasons for attrition, but the most common appear to be transportation, scheduling conflicts with work, and loss of contact after a change of address or phone number.

*Clinical results.* Among completers, average HbA1c fell from 9.1 percent at enrollment to 7.8 percent at twelve months, a reduction of 1.3 points. A reduction of that size is clinically meaningful and consistent with published results for structured self-management programs. Two cautions: these figures describe completers only, so they likely overstate the effect for the enrolled population as a whole, and we do not yet have follow-up data on whether improvements hold after patients exit the program.

*Cost.* At $185,000, the program cost roughly $450 per enrollee and roughly $690 per completer.

**3. What each option would cost**

The figures below are planning estimates. I can provide line-item budgets on request.

| Option | Estimated annual cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Renew at current staffing** | $190,000–$195,000 | Two nurse educators, one part-time dietitian, supplies, and modest cost-of-living adjustments. Continues service to roughly 400 patients per year at the Dover site. |
| **Expand to Milford satellite** | $290,000–$305,000 | Adds one nurse educator based at Milford, increases dietitian hours to full-time, and covers travel, space, and equipment. Would add an estimated 150–200 enrollees per year. |
| **Wind down** | $15,000–$25,000 one-time | Covers patient transition to primary care, referral to outside programs, grant close-out reporting, and staff notice periods. Eliminates ongoing cost after June 30. |

Under any renewal option, the committee should assume that the expiring grant is not guaranteed. I have inquired with the state about a renewal cycle and will report as soon as I have a response.

**4. What the committee needs to decide**

Before the grant lapses on June 30, the committee needs to decide:

1. **Which option to pursue** — renewal, expansion, or wind-down.
2. **How a renewed or expanded program would be funded** — whether through a new state grant application, other grants, operating reserves, or a combination, and whether the center is willing to bridge-fund the program if a new grant decision comes after June 30.
3. **A decision date.** Our nurse educators will begin looking for other positions if their roles are uncertain past the spring. I recommend the committee reach a decision no later than the end of March so that I can either begin grant applications and recruitment or begin an orderly transition of patients.

I would also ask the committee to consider, as part of any renewal, a modest investment in retention — for example, transportation assistance or telephone follow-up — since the 35 percent who leave early represent the largest gap between what the program could deliver and what it currently does.

I am available to meet with the committee at its convenience and will bring detailed budgets and patient-level data to that discussion.
